title: Customer traveling abroad pays for dinner on their usual phone
narrative: The customer pays $86.40 at a restaurant. The IP resolves to London or Berlin while the billing address is in the US, without any VPN or Tor. The phone is the one they have used for at least six months, and the amount and frequency are normal for them.
rationale: A trusted device used abroad for an ordinary purchase is normal travel. A location mismatch on its own, with no anonymization and no device change, does not justify friction.
